# Avatar group: `jl-avatar-group`

A few people at a glance: overlapping avatars, and a count for the others.

- Class `JlAvatarGroup`, a molecule: `import { JlAvatarGroup } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/avatar-group

An avatar group shows who is in something (a project, a document, a call) in little room. The avatars
overlap, each ringed with the surface colour so they stay apart.

With max, the group shows that many avatars and a last one that counts the others; its tooltip names them, and screen
readers hear them. Set --ring-color when the group sits on another background than the surface.

## Use

```ts
import { JlAvatarGroup } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlAvatarGroup
  items={[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]}
  max={4}
  size="lg"
/>
```

```html
<jl-avatar-group
  items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'
  max="4"
  size="lg"
></jl-avatar-group>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `items` (attribute `items`): `AvatarItem[]`, default `[]`. The people, in order: [{ "name": "Ada Lovelace", "src": "/ada.jpg" }].
- `max` (attribute `max`): `number`, default `0`. How many avatars show before the count; 0 shows them all.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'`, default `'md'`. The size of every avatar: 24, 32, 40 or 56 pixels.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The row of avatars.
- `--overlap` (custom property): How far each avatar slides under the one before.
- `--ring-color` (custom property): The ring between avatars: the background the group sits on.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### With a max

Seven people, four shown: the last avatar counts the three others.

```html
<jl-avatar-group max="4" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
```

### Sizes

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-avatar-group size="sm" max="5" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
  <jl-avatar-group size="md" max="5" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
  <jl-avatar-group size="lg" max="5" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
  <jl-avatar-group size="xl" max="3" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
</div>
```

### Pictures

Pictures and initials mix; without max, everyone shows.

```html
<jl-avatar-group size="lg" items='[{"name":"Barbara Liskov"},{"name":"jlib","src":"favicon.svg"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
```

### Beside a sentence

Who works on a project, next to what they did.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-avatar-group size="sm" max="3" items='[{"name":"Ada Lovelace"},{"name":"Grace Hopper"},{"name":"Alan Turing"},{"name":"Margaret Hamilton"},{"name":"Linus Torvalds"},{"name":"Radia Perlman"},{"name":"Ken Thompson"}]'></jl-avatar-group>
  <span class="muted">Ada, Grace and 5 others edited this page today</span>
</div>
```
